summary: Johannes Nobel worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Greifswald and Berlin, earning his PhD under Heinrich Lüders. He held posts at the Prussian State Library, Berlin, and Marburg, where he was Lehrstuhl für Indologie (1928–1955).

Johannes Rahder was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Japanology. After earning his doctorate at Utrecht University, he held chairs and professorships at Utrecht (1930–1931), Leiden (1931–1946), the University of Hawaiʻi, and Yale University (1947–1965).

Johannes Schmidt was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Bonn and Jena, completing his doctorate under August Schleicher and studying under Albrecht Weber. He served as professor at Bonn (1868), Graz (1873–1876), and Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1876).

Johannes Schneider works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Marburg, he held posts at Freie Universität Berlin, the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the University of Munich, where he became apl. Professor in 2014.

Johannes Schubert specialized in Tibetology and Sinology. He studied at the University of Leipzig and under scholars including August Conrady and Erich Haenisch. His career included roles at Leipzig University Library (1927–1954) and teaching Tibetology at the University of Leipzig.

John A. Ardussi specializes in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He completed an MA under Turrell V. Wylie, earned his PhD at the Australian National University, and served as a research team member at CNRS.
John A. Brinkman is a historian and archaeologist. He held long-term posts at the University of Chicago (circa 1963–2004) and served as a professor at the University of Oxford (attested 1999).

John Alexander Stewart was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. Educated at the University of Aberdeen, he served in the Indian Civil Service (circa 1905–1933) before becoming Reader in Burmese at the University of London and serving at SOAS (circa 1933–1948).

John Allan was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. Educated at Edinburgh and Leipzig, he served as Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (from 1931) and lectured in Sanskrit at UCL, SOAS, and the University of Edinburgh.

John Avery was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Amherst College, Tübingen, Berlin, and under William Dwight Whitney. He later served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College (1870–1877) and Bowdoin College (1877).
John B. Carman specialized in Indology and religious studies. He served as faculty at Harvard University and was Director of the Center for the Study of World Religions.

John B. Cobb Jr. is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. After earning his PhD at the University of Chicago, he served as a professor at Claremont Graduate University and Claremont School of Theology, and co-founded the Center for Process Studies.

John Berthrong specialized in Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied for his graduate degree under Alfonso Verdu and served on the faculty at Boston University from circa 1989 to 2013.

John Borthwick Gilchrist was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh. He served in the East India Company, was principal of Fort William College (1800–1804), and became the first Professor of Hindustani at University College London.
John Brockington is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh (attested in 1987 and 2003).

John Brough was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Edinburgh and Cambridge under Arthur Berriedale Keith and Harold Walter Bailey, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London and later as professor at Cambridge (1967–1984).
John Buescher is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia in 1982 and served as Director at Voice of America.
John Burnet was a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. He held an academic post at the University of St Andrews from circa 1892 to 1926.

John Burton-Page specialized in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the Royal College of Music and the University of Oxford, later holding posts at Deccan College and SOAS University of London (circa 1953–1984).
John C. Huntington was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He served as a professor at Ohio State University (attested 1987–2000).
